option_deterrence_top_of_block.highlight: Session focus: top-of-block ordering to prioritize trustworthy key revealers; untrusted publishers relegated to bottom of priority section, still above public mempool
Jannik opened PR to Lucid spec adding a validator-voted priority list for key publishers; voting weighted by effective balance, recomputed per epoch
Key messages now require signatures to prevent impersonation of priority-listed publishers; BLS unsuitable since key publishers are EL addresses — signing scheme unresolved
max-preceding-commitments removed from Lucid to avoid conflict with new priority-list ordering; authors' feedback requested
Top-of-block fee retained for congestion control within the priority section; ordering inside that section remains fee-based, not key-publisher-trust-based, to avoid collusion effects

key_publisher_governance.highlight: No automatic slashing for invalid key reveals; validators must manually vote publishers out — external monitoring software proposed to assist
Permissionless entry model: new publishers operate outside priority section, build reputation, then get voted in by validators

action_items.action: Review Lucid PR (shutter-network/EIPs#1); focus on Engine API changes and priority-list propagation from EL to CL
Escalate optionality concerns and priority-list PR to Tama for review
Review Lucid priority-list PR and provide comments; consult local CL contacts

decisions.decision: Top-of-block fee kept; ordering within priority section remains fee-based (not trust-rank-based)
Priority section admission is binary (≥50% validator support = in), not ranked by degree of trust
